correctness.rationale: Starting from the source Eq. (23), direct expansion of the rank-one factor \(R_x=I+xx^{\mathsf T}/(1-\|x\|^2)\) gives exactly \(4J_B=R_x(D+D^{\mathsf T})R_x\). For \(\|x\|<1\), \(R_x\) is positive definite and invertible, with eigenvalues \(1,1,(1-\|x\|^2)^{-1}\). Sylvester congruence therefore preserves the complete inertia, so positivity of the Bures/Fisher local growth form is equivalent to the source trace-distance condition. The specialization to the source example follows because every diagonal entry of its finite-time damping matrix is strictly negative.
risks: The theorem is local to the full-rank Bloch ball; no claim is made about finite state separations or integrated witness magnitudes.
The checker is only a consistency test; the universal result rests on the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The result closes an explicit numerical step in a widely cited non-Markovianity analysis and reveals a structural fact stronger than that single example: throughout the unital qubit regime the local Bures/Fisher and trace-distance witness forms have the same complete inertia. This explains exactly why changing between these two local distinguishability geometries cannot recover non-Markovianity missed by the trace-distance criterion in that regime.
risks: The theorem does not improve detection beyond trace distance for unital qubits; its value is the exact equivalence and the resulting no-advantage statement, not a new stronger detector.
The statement is dimension-specific and does not address non-unital translations.
